st: Lay the eggplant slices on trays and sprinkle with [[1 tsp]] salt. Let sit 20 minutes, then pat dry with paper towels.
Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Brush the slices with [[0.5 cup]] olive oil in total and roast on lined trays for 25 minutes, flipping once, until golden. Lower the oven to 350°F (175°C).
Brown the lamb in a large pan over medium-high heat for 8 minutes, breaking it up. Add the onion and garlic and cook 5 minutes.
Add the wine (or water), tomatoes, cinnamon, oregano, [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper. Simmer for 20 minutes until thick.
Make the bechamel: melt the butter in a pot, whisk in the flour and cook 2 minutes. Slowly whisk in the milk and cook, stirring, about 8 minutes until thick.
Off the heat, whisk in the nutmeg, [[0.5 tsp]] salt and the cheese. Let cool 5 minutes, then whisk in the egg yolks.
In a 9x13 inch dish, layer half the eggplant, all the meat sauce, then the remaining eggplant.
Pour the bechamel over the top and smooth it out.
Bake for 40 minutes until the top is golden and bubbling.
Rest for 20 minutes before cutting so the layers set.
Mix the lemon juice, [[0.25 cup]] olive oil, oregano, garlic, [[1.5 tsp]] salt and the pepper in a bowl.
Add the pork, toss well, cover and marinate in the fridge for at least 2 hours.
If using wooden skewers, soak 8 of them in water for 30 minutes. Thread the pork onto the skewers.
Heat a grill or cast-iron pan over medium-high heat and oil it lightly.
Cook the skewers for 10 to 12 minutes, turning every few minutes, until browned and the pork reaches 145°F (63°C).
Warm the pita on the grill for 30 seconds per side.
Slide the meat off the skewers into the pita with tomato, onion and tzatziki, and roll up.
Mix the olive oil, half the garlic, oregano, paprika, cumin, lemon juice, [[1.5 tsp]] salt and the pepper. Coat the pork slices and marinate for at least 1 hour.
Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the potato fries with the vegetable oil and a pinch of salt, and spread on a tray.
Roast the potatoes for 30 minutes, turning once, until crisp and golden.
Stir the yogurt with the remaining garlic and a pinch of salt for a quick sauce.
Heat a large skillet over high heat. Cook the pork in batches for 3 to 4 minutes per batch until browned at the edges and cooked through to 145°F (63°C).
Warm the pita in a dry pan or the oven.
Fill each pita with pork, tomato, onion, a few fries and the yogurt sauce, then fold and serve.

ing: washed and chopped, or 20 oz frozen, thawed and squeezed dry
st: Heat [[2 tbsp]] olive oil in a large pan and cook the onion and green onions for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the fresh spinach in handfuls and cook until wilted, about 4 minutes. Transfer to a colander and press out as much liquid as you can, then let cool.
In a big bowl, mix the spinach, feta, eggs, dill, nutmeg, pepper and salt.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Brush a 9x13 inch pan with olive oil.
Lay a sheet of phyllo in the pan and brush with olive oil. Repeat until you have 10 layers, keeping the unused sheets under a damp towel.
Spread the spinach filling over the layers evenly.
Top with 10 more oiled phyllo sheets, brushing each. Brush the top with the remaining oil and score the top layers into squares.
Bake for 45 minutes until deep golden and crisp.
Cool 15 minutes, then cut along the scored lines.
Cut the tomatoes into wedges and put them in a wide bowl.
Add the cucumber, red onion, olives and bell pepper rings if using.
Sprinkle with [[0.5 tsp]] salt and the vinegar, then drizzle with half of the [[0.25 cup]] olive oil. Toss gently.
Place the slab of feta on top.
Sprinkle the feta with the oregano and drizzle with the remaining olive oil.
Serve right away with crusty bread to mop up the juices.
Boil the pasta in well-salted water for 2 minutes less than the package says. Drain, toss with [[2 tbsp]] of the butter and half the eggs.
Heat the olive oil in a large pan. Cook the onion for 5 minutes, then add the garlic and beef. Brown the beef well for 8 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste, crushed tomatoes, cinnamon, [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper. Simmer for 20 minutes until thick.
Make the bechamel: melt [[4 tbsp]] butter in a pot, whisk in the flour and cook for 2 minutes. Slowly whisk in the milk and cook about 8 minutes until thick.
Off the heat, stir in [[0.5 cup]] cheese, the nutmeg, [[1 tsp]] salt and the remaining beaten egg.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Spread half the pasta in a 9x13 inch dish, then all the meat sauce, then the rest of the pasta.
Pour the bechamel over the top and sprinkle with the remaining [[0.5 cup]] cheese.
Bake for 40 minutes until the top is golden. Rest 15 minutes before cutting.
Rinse the grape leaves in warm water and trim off any hard stems. Set aside a few torn leaves.
Heat [[0.25 cup]] olive oil in a pan and cook the onion and green onions for 5 minutes. Add the rice and stir 2 minutes.
Off the heat, mix in the dill, mint, juice of 1 lemon, salt and pepper. Let cool.
Place a leaf shiny side down, with the stem end toward you. Put a heaping teaspoon of filling near the stem end.
Fold in the sides, then roll up tightly like a small cigar. Repeat with all leaves.
Line a heavy pot with the torn leaves. Pack the rolls seam side down in tight layers.
Pour over [[2 cups]] hot water, the remaining lemon juice and [[0.25 cup]] olive oil. Set a plate on top to keep them from unrolling.
Cover and simmer on low for 45 minutes until the rice is tender.
Cool in the pot. Serve at room temperature or chilled with lemon.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Scoop the pulp out of the tomatoes and chop it, saving the juices. Hollow out the peppers.
Heat [[0.25 cup]] olive oil in a pan and cook the onion for 5 minutes, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the chopped tomato pulp and cook 8 minutes. Stir in the rice, tomato paste, sugar, [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper. Cook 2 minutes.
Off the heat, stir in the parsley and mint.
Sprinkle the inside of the tomatoes and peppers with a pinch of salt. Fill them about three-quarters full, since the rice will swell.
Stand them upright in a baking dish, snug together, with the potato wedges in the gaps. Put the tops back on.
Pour [[0.5 cup]] water around them and drizzle with the remaining [[0.25 cup]] olive oil and [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Bake for 60 to 70 minutes, basting once, until the rice is tender and the edges brown.
Rest 15 minutes and serve warm or at room temperature.
Put the chicken, onion, carrot, celery and [[8 cups]] water in a pot. Bring to a boil, skim off any foam, then simmer for 30 minutes until the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C).
Lift out the chicken and strain the broth back into the pot. Discard the vegetables.
Season the broth with [[1.5 tsp]] salt and the pepper. Add the rice and simmer for 15 minutes until tender.
Shred the chicken, discarding the skin and bones.
Whisk the eggs in a bowl until frothy, then whisk in the lemon juice.
Slowly ladle about [[1 cup]] of hot broth into the eggs, whisking constantly so they do not scramble.
Turn the heat to low. Stir the egg mixture into the pot and add the chicken. Heat gently for 3 minutes without boiling.
Taste, add salt or lemon, sprinkle with dill, and serve right away.
Drain the soaked beans and put them in a large pot with fresh water to cover. Boil for 10 minutes, then drain and rinse.
In the clean pot, heat [[0.33 cup]] olive oil over medium heat. Cook the onion, carrots and celery for 8 minutes.
Add the garlic and tomato paste and stir for 1 minute.
Add the beans, tomatoes, bay leaves, oregano and [[8 cups]] fresh water. Bring to a boil.
Lower the heat, partly cover and simmer for 1 hour 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until the beans are very soft.
Add [[2 tsp]] salt and the pepper and simmer 10 minutes more, until the soup is thick.
Discard the bay leaves. Serve topped with parsley and a drizzle of olive oil.
Grate the cucumber on a box grater and sprinkle with a pinch of the salt. Let it sit for 5 minutes.
Squeeze the cucumber hard in a clean towel to remove as much water as you can.
Put the yogurt in a bowl and stir in the cucumber.
Add the garlic, [[2 tbsp]] olive oil, dill and [[1 tbsp]] lemon juice.
Season with the remaining salt and the pepper and stir well.
Chill for at least 1 hour so the flavors blend, then serve with a drizzle of olive oil.
Make the syrup: boil [[1 cup]] sugar, [[1 cup]] water, the honey and lemon juice for 10 minutes. Cool completely.
Mix the walnuts with [[0.25 cup]] sugar, the cinnamon and cloves.
Heat the oven to 325°F (165°C). Brush a 9x13 inch pan with melted butter.
Lay a phyllo sheet in the pan, brush with butter, and repeat until you have 8 sheets.
Spread a third of the nut mix, then add 3 buttered sheets. Repeat twice more, finishing with the remaining nuts.
Add the last 5 buttered sheets on top and brush with all the remaining butter.
Cut into diamonds or squares with a sharp knife before baking, all the way through.
Bake for 50 minutes until deep golden.
Pour the cooled syrup evenly over the hot baklava right when it comes out.
Let it soak for at least 4 hours before serving.
Stir the yeast and sugar into the warm water. Let sit for 5 minutes until foamy.
Whisk the flour and salt in a large bowl. Pour in the yeast water and mix into a very soft, sticky batter.
Cover and let rise in a warm spot for 1 hour until doubled and bubbly.
Warm the honey with [[2 tbsp]] water and the lemon juice in a small pot, then keep it warm.
Heat [[4 cups]] oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Wet a spoon, scoop a walnut-sized blob of batter, and push it into the oil with another spoon. Fry 6 at a time.
Fry for 3 to 4 minutes, turning, until deep golden and puffed. Drain on paper towels.
Pile onto a plate, drizzle with the warm honey and sprinkle with cinnamon and walnuts. Serve at once.
Take the cheeses out of the fridge 20 minutes before serving. Pat the feta dry with paper towels so it does not make the board wet.
Set the feta slab on one side of a large board, drizzle with [[2 tbsp]] olive oil and sprinkle with [[1 tsp]] oregano.
Cut the graviera into thin wedges and slice the loukaniko into coins. Lay the pastourma slices in a loose fold beside them.
Spoon the tzatziki into a bowl and swirl the top. Pour [[1 tbsp]] oil over it. Put the olives in a second bowl.
Slice the cucumber into rounds and halve the tomatoes, then tuck them around the bowls to fill the gaps with color.
Cut the pita into wedges. Warm them in a dry skillet for 1 minute per side if you like, then stack them at the end of the board and serve.
nt: Don't cook (pita optionally warmed): slice, fold, arrange; cheeses at room temperature 20 minutes
Best swap: halloumi or ricotta salata for graviera, and marinated dolmades or fried vegetables in place of the meats for a vegetarian board.

st: Mix [[4 cup]] flour, [[0.5 cup]] sugar, [[2.25 tsp]] yeast, [[1 tsp]] mahleb and [[0.5 tsp]] mastic in a bowl.
Add [[0.75 cup]] warm milk, [[0.5 cup]] melted butter, 2 eggs, 1 yolk and orange zest. Knead 12 minutes to a soft, slightly sticky dough.
Cover and rise 2 hours in a warm place until doubled.
Divide into 3 equal pieces. Roll each into a 20 inch rope and braid them, tucking the ends under. Place on a lined tray.
Rise another 45 minutes. Heat the oven to 350°F. Brush with beaten egg and top with sliced almonds if you like.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes until deep golden, covering loosely with foil if it browns too quickly. Cool on a rack.
nt: Baked at 350°F
Best swap: if you cannot find mahleb or mastic, use 1 tsp ground anise and a drop of vanilla.

st: Heat the milk in a large pot until steaming. Whisk in the semolina and custard sugar and stir for 8 minutes over medium heat until thick like pudding.
Remove from the heat. Whisk the eggs in a bowl, then slowly stir in a ladle of hot custard to warm them, and pour it all back into the pot.
Stir over low heat for 3 minutes so the eggs cook through, then add the vanilla and cool 10 minutes.
Heat the oven to 350°F. Brush a 9 by 13 inch pan with butter. Layer in 6 phyllo sheets, brushing each with butter.
Pour in the custard, then top with the remaining 6 sheets, brushing each with butter. Score the top into squares.
Bake for 45 minutes until deep golden and puffed.
Boil the syrup sugar, [[1 cup]] water and the lemon peel for 8 minutes. Cool, then pour over the hot pastry and let it soak 1 hour.
nt: Baked at 350°F, then syrup-soaked
Best swap: use cornstarch, 1 if you cannot find it.

ing: ground with a pinch of sugar
st: Grind the mastic with [[1 tbsp]] of the sugar in a mortar until a fine powder. This stops it sticking.
Whisk the cornstarch with [[0.25 cup]] cold milk until smooth. Heat the rest of the milk, cream, remaining sugar and salep in a pot until steaming.
Whisk in the cornstarch slurry and cook over medium-low heat, stirring, until it coats a spoon and bubbles gently, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the mastic sugar and vanilla. Cool the base, then chill in the fridge until very cold, at least 4 hours.
Churn in an ice cream maker until thick and stretchy, about 25 minutes.
Freeze in a covered container for 2 hours to firm up, then scoop and serve with spoon sweets or cherries.
nt: Cooked custard base, churned
Best swap: no ice cream maker, freeze the base and whisk it hard every 45 minutes 3 times. Skip salep if you cannot find it.

st: Put the octopus in a pot with the bay leaves, cover with cold water and bring to a simmer. Do not add salt.
Cover and simmer gently 45 to 60 minutes, until a knife slides easily into the thickest part of the tentacle.
Drain, cool, and cut into 3 or 4 inch pieces, keeping the tentacles whole. Pat dry. Toss with [[1 tbsp]] oil.
Heat a grill to high, about 500°F, and oil the grate.
Grill the pieces 3 to 4 minutes per side without moving until charred at the edges.
Whisk [[3 tbsp]] oil with [[1 tbsp]] vinegar, the juice of the lemons, oregano and garlic. Pour over the hot octopus, season with flaky salt and serve.
nt: Simmered tender first, then charred over high grill heat
Best swap: sear in a very hot cast iron pan 3 minutes per side. Use squid steaks, grilled 2 minutes per side, in place of octopus.

st: Soak the beans in plenty of cold water for 8 hours or overnight. Drain.
Cover the beans with fresh water in a large pot, bring to a boil, then simmer for 45 minutes until nearly tender. Drain, saving [[1 cup]] of the cooking liquid.
Heat the oven to 350°F. Warm [[0.25 cup]] olive oil in a pan over medium heat and cook the onion, carrot and celery for 8 minutes until soft.
Stir in the garlic, [[2 tbsp]] tomato paste and oregano for 1 minute, then add the crushed tomatoes, [[1 tsp]] salt and the saved cooking liquid. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Mix the beans, sauce, dill and parsley in a large baking dish. Pour [[0.25 cup]] olive oil over the top.
Bake uncovered, stirring once or twice, until the sauce is thick and the beans are creamy and slightly crisped on top, about 55 minutes.
Rest for 10 minutes. Serve warm or room temperature with bread and feta if you eat dairy.
nt: Boiled, then baked at 350°F
Best swap: use two 15 oz cans of drained butter beans or large lima beans and skip the first two steps.

st: Heat the oven to 375°F. Toss the potatoes, zucchini, eggplant, onion and garlic in a big bowl with [[1.5 tsp]] salt, the pepper and oregano.
Spread the vegetables in a large roasting dish in an even, slightly overlapping layer.
Mix the grated tomatoes with [[0.5 cup]] olive oil and pour them over the top.
Bake uncovered for 45 minutes, then stir gently from the edges.
Bake another 30 to 40 minutes until the potatoes are tender and the top is browned in spots. Add a little water if the pan looks dry.
Sprinkle with parsley and rest 10 minutes before serving.
nt: Roasted at 375°F
Best swap: add 1 cup sliced green beans, or use sweet potato for half the potatoes.

st: Grate the tomatoes on the large holes of a box grater into a bowl, leaving the skins behind in your hand. Discard the skins.
Stir a pinch of salt into the grated tomato and let it drain in a sieve for 5 minutes so the topping is not too wet.
Place the rusks on a platter. Sprinkle each with a spoon of water or tomato juice, about [[1 tbsp]], so they soften slightly but stay crunchy in the center.
Spoon the grated tomato over each rusk, covering it to the edges.
Crumble the feta on top and scatter the olives and capers over the plates.
Sprinkle with oregano, drizzle with [[4 tbsp]] olive oil and let sit for 5 minutes before eating so the rusk can soften.
nt: Don't cook: grated and assembled
Best swap: crushed whole wheat crispbread or hard sourdough toast if you cannot find barley rusks.

st: Heat the oven to 350°F. Grease and flour a 10 inch round pan.
Beat the butter and [[1 cup]] sugar for 5 minutes until pale. Beat in the egg yolks one at a time, then the zest.
Mix the flour, baking powder and mastic. Add to the batter in 3 parts, alternating with the orange juice and milk.
Whip the whites with the remaining [[0.25 cup]] sugar to stiff peaks and fold into the batter in 2 parts.
Pour into the pan and press the foil-wrapped coin into the batter anywhere. Scatter the almonds on top.
Bake for 45 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean. Cool for 15 minutes, then turn out.
Dust with powdered sugar. Cut slices for the household in order, and warn guests about the coin.
nt: Baked at 350°F
Best swap: lemon zest and juice for orange in equal amounts; skip mastic or use 0.5 tsp vanilla.

st: Beat the butter for 8 minutes until very white and fluffy. This is what makes the cookies melt in the mouth.
Add [[0.5 cup]] powdered sugar, the egg yolk, brandy and vanilla and beat 2 more minutes.
Fold in the flour, baking powder and almonds until a soft dough forms. Chill for 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 350°F. Shape the dough into crescents or balls about 1.5 inches wide and place on lined trays.
Bake for 18 minutes until pale gold on the bottom. They should not brown on top.
Brush the warm cookies lightly with [[1 tbsp]] rose water if using, then sift [[0.5 cup]] powdered sugar over them.
Cool completely, then dust generously with the remaining [[1 cup]] powdered sugar before serving.
nt: Baked at 350°F
Best swap: use vegan butter in equal weight and 2 tbsp cold milk in place of the yolk.

st: Tear the bread into pieces and soak in the water for 2 minutes, then squeeze out the excess. It should feel like wet dough.
Pound or blend the garlic with the salt until it forms a smooth paste with no visible pieces.
Add the almonds and the squeezed bread to the garlic and mix until a thick, uniform paste forms.
With the food processor running or while whisking hard, drizzle in the olive oil in a thin stream so the mixture turns pale and creamy.
Stir in [[2 tbsp]] red wine vinegar. Taste and add more salt or a splash of water if it is too thick to scoop.
Rest for 15 minutes so the garlic mellows, then serve at room temperature with fried fish or roasted beets.
nt: Don't cook: pound or blend, then drizzle in the oil
Best swap: 1 lb boiled, mashed russet potato instead of the bread and almonds for the classic potato version.

st: Soak the bread in the water for 2 minutes, then squeeze it very dry. Discard the soaking water.
Put the tarama and grated onion in a food processor and blend for 30 seconds until smooth.
Add the squeezed bread and blend again until you have a thick, even paste.
With the machine running, slowly pour in the olive oil in a thin stream, alternating with [[0.25 cup]] lemon juice.
Taste. Add a little cold water if it is too stiff. It should be pale pink, light and fluffy.
Chill for 30 minutes and serve with warm pita, cucumber and olives.
nt: Don't cook: blend and emulsify with oil
Best swap: boiled and mashed potato (1 medium) in place of the bread for a gluten-free version.

st: Heat the oven to 350°F. Season the lamb with salt and oregano.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] olive oil in a roasting pan on the stove over medium-high heat. Sear the lamb 4 minutes per side until browned, then remove.
Cook the onion and garlic in the same pan for 5 minutes until soft. Pour in [[0.5 cup]] wine and scrape up the brown bits.
Add the tomatoes, cinnamon, lamb and [[1 cup]] hot broth. Cover tightly with foil and roast for 1 hour 30 minutes until the lamb is nearly tender.
Remove the cinnamon. Stir in the orzo and [[2 cup]] hot broth. Roast uncovered for 25 minutes, stirring once, until the orzo is tender and the sauce thick.
Rest 10 minutes, then sprinkle with the grated cheese and serve from the pan.
nt: Seared, then roasted and braised in the oven
Best swap: use beef chuck or bone-in chicken thighs for the lamb, with 1 hour of covered roasting for chicken.

ing: 3 tbsp to shake, the rest to top up
st: Put [[2 tsp]] instant coffee, [[2 tsp]] sugar and [[3 tbsp]] cold water in a tall shaker or jar with a tight lid.
Shake hard for about 30 seconds, or use a handheld frother for 20 seconds, until you get a thick, pale tan foam that fills the container.
Fill a tall glass with [[1 cup]] ice cubes.
Pour the foam over the ice, letting it settle a moment.
Slowly add about [[0.75 cup]] cold water down the side of the glass, keeping the foam on top.
Stir in [[2 tbsp]] evaporated milk if you like, and serve with a straw.
nt: Don't cook: shaken or frothed over ice
Best swap: [[2 tbsp]] oat milk instead of evaporated milk, and 1 tsp maple syrup for the sugar.

st: Heat the oven to 350°F. Brush a 9 by 13 inch pan with melted butter.
Mash feta and ricotta in a bowl. Beat in the eggs, dill and pepper. Feta is salty so add no extra salt.
Lay a phyllo sheet in the pan, letting it hang over, and brush lightly with butter. Repeat for 8 sheets. Keep the stack under a damp towel while you work.
Spread the cheese filling evenly over the phyllo.
Layer 8 more sheets on top, brushing each with butter. Fold the overhang over the top and brush with butter.
Cut through the top layers into squares with a sharp knife before baking so it does not shatter.
Bake 45 minutes until deep golden and puffed and the center feels set. The eggs should reach 160°F inside.
Rest 10 minutes, then cut through again and serve warm or at room temperature.
nt: Baked at 350°F
Best swap: use cottage cheese strained of liquid 1 to 1 in place of ricotta; swap olive oil for butter for a vegan-friendly layer, with a tofu filling.
